chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

I asked him about a man who divorces his wife with one or two divorces, then leaves her until her waiting period expires. What is her status? He said: If he leaves her intending not to remarry her, she becomes fully divorced from him and is not permissible to him until she marries another husband. And if he leaves her intending to remarry her, and a year passes, then he has more right to her revocation (of the divorce).

key_terms.رَجْعَة: Right of revocation (taking back the wife)
key_terms.عِدَّة: Waiting period for a divorced woman
key_terms.مُرَاجَعَة: Remarriage/revocation of divorce without a new contract

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband divorces his wife once or twice and then waits for her waiting period to expire?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) clarifies the distinction between a revocable divorce (raj'i) and an irrevocable one (ba'in) based on the husband's intent during the waiting period. It highlights the Shia juristic view that if the husband delays remarriage for a year after the 'iddah' expires while intending to return, he retains the right of revocation without a new contract, a nuance often discussed in contrast to Sunni schools regarding the expiration of the waiting period.
